walkthrough:
Integrate $y$ with respect to $x$ using the reverse chain rule:
$$\int y\,dx = 3\left( \frac{(4x + 1)^{3/2}}{\frac{3}{2} \times 4} \right) - \frac{2x^2}{2} + c = \frac{1}{2}(4x + 1)^{3/2} - x^2 + c$$

State the two calculus expressions:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{6}{\sqrt{4x + 1}} - 2, \quad \int y\,dx = \frac{1}{2}(4x + 1)^{3/2} - x^2 + c$$

Set $\frac{dy}{dx} = 0$ to find the $x$-coordinate of the stationary point $M$:
$$\frac{6}{\sqrt{4x + 1}} - 2 = 0 \implies \frac{6}{\sqrt{4x + 1}} = 2 \implies \sqrt{4x + 1} = 3$$
$$4x + 1 = 9 \implies 4x = 8 \implies x = 2$$

Find the coordinates of $A$ on the $y$-axis ($x = 0$):
$$y = 3\sqrt{4(0) + 1} - 2(0) = 3(1) = 3 \implies A = (0, \, 3)$$

Calculate the area under the curve from $x = 0$ to $x = 2$ using the integral from part (i):
$$\text{Area}_{\text{curve}} = \left[ \frac{1}{2}(4x + 1)^{3/2} - x^2 \right]_0^2 = \left( \frac{1}{2}(9^{3/2}) - 2^2 \right) - \left( \frac{1}{2}(1^{3/2}) - 0 \right)$$
$$\text{Area}_{\text{curve}} = \left( \frac{27}{2} - 4 \right) - \frac{1}{2} = 9.5 - 0.5 = 9$$

Calculate the area of the trapezium formed under the chord $AM$ between $x = 0$ and $x = 2$:
$$\text{Area}_{\text{trapezium}} = \frac{1}{2} \times (y_A + y_M) \times (x_M - x_A) = \frac{1}{2}(3 + 5)(2) = 8$$

Subtract the trapezium area from the curve area to find the shaded area:
$$\text{Shaded Area} = \text{Area}_{\text{curve}} - \text{Area}_{\text{trapezium}} = 9 - 8 = 1$$
